title: Create a new notebook
preconditions: User has access to a JupyterLab workspace
Desired kernel is installed on the server
symptoms: User asks how to create a notebook

diagnostics.description: Check if Launcher tab is open or available via File ➜ New Launcher
Confirm preferred kernel (e.g., Python 3, R) appears in the Launcher

actions.description: Open the Launcher (plus icon on the left sidebar or File ➜ New Launcher)
Select the desired Notebook kernel tile under the Notebook section

payload.summary: Create a new notebook from the launcher
payload.successMessage: New notebook opened in the main area.

actions.description: Rename the untitled notebook via the tab title or File ➜ Rename Notebook

postChecks: Notebook tab appears in main area
Kernel indicator in status bar shows connected state

escalation.condition: Kernel fails to start or is missing

title: Run notebook cells
preconditions: Notebook is open with a connected kernel
symptoms: User unsure how to execute cells

diagnostics.description: Check status bar kernel icon for connection state
Inspect cell toolbar for run button availability

actions.description: Run the current cell with Shift+Enter
Run cell and advance with Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) to stay on the same cell
Use the Run menu ➜ Run Selected Cells or Run All Cells for batch execution
Restart the kernel via Kernel ➜ Restart Kernel if execution stalls

postChecks: Execution count increments next to each executed cell
Kernel status returns to Idle after completion

escalation.contact: Environment maintainer to inspect kernel logs

notes: Keyboard shortcuts reference available via Settings ➜ Advanced Settings ➜ Keyboard Shortcuts

title: Manage kernels

diagnostics.description: Open Kernel menu to view available commands
Check status bar for kernel name and state

actions.description: Restart kernel via Kernel ➜ Restart Kernel to clear state
Change kernel via Kernel ➜ Change Kernel to select another environment
Shut down idle kernels in Kernel ➜ Shut Down All to free resources

postChecks: Kernel name and status reflect the selected environment
Notebook executes cells successfully after restart

escalation.contact: System administrator to install kernel spec

title: Organize files and folders
preconditions: User needs to upload or manage project files
symptoms: Unclear how to create folders or upload files
Need to rename or delete entries

diagnostics.description: Confirm file browser left sidebar is visible (toggle via View ➜ Left Sidebar)

actions.description: Create folders via the file browser toolbar ➜ New Folder icon
Upload files by dragging into the file browser or using the Upload button
Rename, duplicate, or delete via item context menu (right-click)

postChecks: Files appear in desired directory structure

escalation.condition: Upload fails due to size or permissions

title: Use the integrated terminal
preconditions: Shell access to the server is permitted
symptoms: Need to run shell commands alongside notebooks

diagnostics.description: Verify Terminal item exists in Launcher

actions.description: Open Launcher ➜ Terminal tile to start a shell session
Split terminal tab or create additional terminals via + button in the main area
Close terminal sessions via File ➜ Shut Down Terminal to free resources

postChecks: Session appears in Running Terminals list (left sidebar ➜ Running) if active

escalation.condition: Terminal fails to start or displays permission error

title: Use the Command Palette
preconditions: User needs quick access to commands

diagnostics.description: Confirm palette opens with Ctrl+Shift+C (Cmd+Shift+C on macOS) or View ➜ Activate Command Palette

actions.description: Open Command Palette and search for desired command
Pin frequently used commands via right-click ➜ Add to Favorites
Review keyboard shortcuts via Help ➜ Keyboard Shortcuts Reference

escalation.condition: Palette fails to open or commands missing

title: Organize layout and workspaces
preconditions: User wants to save panel arrangement

diagnostics.description: Check current workspace name via URL fragment (e.g., /lab/workspaces/foo)

actions.description: Arrange panels by dragging tabs to new splits
Save current layout via Workspaces menu (Settings ➜ Workspaces ➜ Save Workspace)
Share workspace URL with collaborators if needed

postChecks: Reloading workspace URL restores saved layout

title: Manage extensions
symptoms: Need to install or enable extensions

diagnostics.description: Verify puzzle-piece Extensions icon visible in left sidebar

actions.description: Open Extensions manager and search for required extension
Install or enable extension, acknowledging any security prompts
Reload JupyterLab to activate newly installed extensions

postChecks: Installed extension appears under the Installed tab

escalation.condition: Extension install blocked or fails signature check

diagnostics.description: Confirm nbconvert dependencies installed for PDF/HTML export

actions.description: Use File ➜ Export Notebook As... to choose HTML, Markdown, PDF, or other formats
Download via File ➜ Save and Export Notebook As
Share exported file or publish via shared workspace

escalation.condition: Export fails due to missing LaTeX or nbconvert errors

title: Integrate with Git
symptoms: Need to commit or push changes from JupyterLab

diagnostics.description: Ensure Git extension icon appears in left sidebar

actions.description: Open the Git sidebar to view repository status
Stage changes and compose commit messages within the sidebar
Push or pull via the toolbar buttons; resolve conflicts using diff viewers

escalation.condition: Git extension missing or repository misconfigured
